title: Why Kitchen Sinks Block: The Grease Trap Effect
description: Educational breakdown showing how fats, oils, and grease cool and solidify inside drain P-traps, restricting wastewater flow.
image_prompt: A detailed educational 3D cross-sectional cutaway illustration of a residential kitchen sink drain assembly under a cabinet, vertical 9:16 composition. The main focus is centered on a clean white PVC P-trap fitting. The cutaway section reveals a realistic layer of yellowish-brown solidified grease and fine food debris adhering to the inner curved walls of the trap bend, visibly reducing the internal pipe diameter. Clean water fills the trap seal above the build-up. Background shows a clean, illuminated under-sink cabinet environment with photorealistic textures and natural lighting. No text, no arrows, no watermarks, no logos, no fake branding.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway view of a standard kitchen P-trap to show the exact point where drain blockages typically begin. Viewers can see how warm grease, which enters the sink as a liquid, cools down upon contacting standing water in the trap dip. The visual highlights the physical restriction inside the pipe, demonstrating why grease does not simply wash away down the sewer line.

on_image_text.hook: Why Hot Grease Causes Cold Drain Blockages
on_image_text.explanation: Liquid fats cool rapidly inside wastewater traps, adhering to pipe walls and catching solid debris.
on_image_text.takeaway: Wipe greasy cookware with paper towels before washing to protect your drain line.
